For the lemma, distinct divisors contribute no coefficient mass to one another, and monotone convergence preserves this for the countable finite-mass sum. Local smooth correction and the closed-current restriction theorem give nu(v,D_j)=c_j; the restriction theorem matches [Demailly, Lemma 2.17(b) and Formula 2.18](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/analmeth_book.pdf). For T=Lambda+ddc a, smooth correction preserves its coefficient measures on divisors. Subtracting the prescribed finite divisorial mass leaves a positive restriction to the complement plus nonnegative excess coefficients. Passing to the current limit gives T-S>=0 without assuming T is closed. Thus the L1 difference a-v has a qpsh representative; compactness bounds it above, and canonical local averages give domination everywhere. The ordinary-to-ideal implication and the all-positive-weight ideal-to-Lelong implication have the correct directions.

For the corollary, the allowed decomposition theorem supplies v, and elliptic regularity makes differences of representatives smooth. The cited projection theorem places Q in PSH(Y,Omega), below zero, with all ideals preserved and Q>=v-sup v. The proved lemma supplies Q preceq v, so Q is ordinarily equivalent to v and admissible for P. Together with P<=Q this proves P=Q.

The Gauduchon input applies separately on each fixed model. No uniform mass bound or realization of all future trace coefficients follows. The final caveat is valid: additional unbounded sublogarithmic singularities can preserve every multiplier ideal while changing ordinary type. The curve-fibration reference remains contextual.
